title: The augmented free complex of a hypercover
statement:
Let $U\to X$ be a split etale hypercover
[def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover]. Write $\mathbb Z[V]$ for the
sheafification of the free abelian presheaf on the sheaf represented by an
etale $X$-scheme $V$. Then the alternating-face augmented complex

$$
 \cdots\longrightarrow\mathbb Z[U_2]\longrightarrow
 \mathbb Z[U_1]\longrightarrow\mathbb Z[U_0]
 \longrightarrow\mathbb Z[X]\longrightarrow0
$$

is exact. For an injective abelian sheaf $I$, its complex of sections
consequently satisfies $H^0(C^\bullet(U,I))=I(X)$ and
$H^p(C^\bullet(U,I))=0$ for $p>0$. The same assertions hold with free modules
over a constant ring.

proof.text: Apply the representable presheaf $h_-$ to the augmented simplicial etale $X$-scheme $U$. The matching-cover condition in [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover] says that $h_{U_0}\to h_X$, $h_{U_1}\to h_{U_0}\times_{h_X}h_{U_0}$, and $h_{U_{n+1}}\to(\operatorname{cosk}_n\operatorname{sk}_n h_U)_{n+1}$ for $n\geq1$ become surjective after sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Indeed a section over $W$ of any matching presheaf is a map $W\to M_n(U)$; the pullback $W\times_{M_n(U)}U_n\to W$ is an etale cover, and its tautological lift is a local preimage. The degree-zero comparison object $K^0$ has degree $m$ equal to the $(m+1)$-fold fibre product of $h_{U_0}$ over $h_X$. Its augmented free-module complex has positive homology zero and degree-zero homology $R[h_X]^\#$ by [lem-weil-pbc-cech-nerve-free-homology], taking $F=h_{U_0}$ and $G=h_X$.

For $n\geq1$ put $K^n=\operatorname{cosk}_n\operatorname{sk}_n h_U$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton]. The map $K^n\to K^{n-1}$ is an isomorphism below degree $n$ and its degree-$n$ map is the $n$th matching map of $U$ [lem-weil-pbc-matching-object-coskeleton]. The latter is locally surjective by step 1. Both objects are $n$-coskeletal (an $(n-1)$-coskeletal object is also $n$-coskeletal). Thus [lem-weil-pbc-coskeleton-free-homology-comparison] identifies all free-module homology sheaves of $K^n$ and $K^{n-1}$. By induction they are those of $K^0$.

For fixed $i$, the homology in degree $i$ of the alternating-face complex depends only on terms and faces through degree $i+1$. These agree for $h_U$ and $K^{i+1}$. Hence step 2 transfers the vanishing of positive homology and the degree-zero identification from $K^0$ to $h_U$. In degree zero the map is precisely the given augmentation, so the whole augmented free-$R$ complex is exact. The argument applies to every commutative constant coefficient ring $R$, including $R=\mathbb Z$; it uses the free-$R$ statements of the two preceding lemmas directly, with no tensor-exactness assumption on $R$.

For an etale $X$-scheme $V$ and an injective abelian sheaf $I$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], the sheafification adjunction [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] and the free-presheaf Yoneda equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module] (with the constant ring $\mathbb Z$) identify $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb Z[V],I)$ with $I(V)$. Applying $\operatorname{Hom}(-,I)$ to the exact augmented complex from step 3 is exact by the defining extension property of an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Thus the resulting cochain complex has $H^0=I(X)$ and $H^p=0$ for $p>0$. The same adjunction and injectivity argument in the category of sheaves of modules over a constant commutative ring gives the module assertion.

Its second paragraph identifies Hom from the free sheaf to an injective with sections and applies injectivity; step 4 realizes it.
